insights.headline: Gold pinned near $4,150 as 24-year-high yields trump soft PCE; festive silver demand a bright spot
insights.summary: Gold held near $4,150 as the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.304%, a 24-year high, and the dollar wrapped its best month since March — overwhelming relief from cooler August PCE inflation. October Fed-hike odds sit near 37%, with Friday's US jobs report the next test. For Indian buyers, record gold prices are pushing festive shoppers toward silver, up 160% in two years, while the rupee is expected to weaken further in H2FY27 and MCX bullion steadied near ₹1.50 lakh.
points: Gold near $4,150 as 10-yr yield hit 5.304% (24-yr high) and 30-yr ~5.65%; October Fed-hike odds ~37%.
Dollar wrapped its best month since March; rupee seen weakening further in H2FY27, yield curve to rise.
Record gold prices are pushing India's festive buyers toward silver — up 160% in two years.
September was brutal: gold -8.5%, silver -13.5% as real yields repriced at the fastest pace in 4 years.
Banks split: Natixis sees $4,100 by year-end on oil and rate pressure; Morgan Stanley still sees $5,000+ in H2 2027.

trending.title: Yields win the standoff: gold at $4,150
trending.summary: A 24-year-high 10-year yield and the dollar's best month since March pinned gold near $4,150 despite soft PCE inflation. October Fed-hike odds near 37%.

trending.title: India's festive pivot: the silver horse
trending.summary: With gold at record highs, India's festive buyers are turning to silver — prices up 160% in two years, with jewellers reporting rising demand from younger buyers.

trending.title: Rupee outlook darkens for H2FY27
trending.summary: IDFC First Bank's chief economist sees the rupee falling further as RBI intervention turns cautious, pushing the G-sec yield curve higher.

trending.title: Banks split on gold's path ahead
trending.summary: Natixis sees gold falling to $4,100 by year-end on oil and rate pressure, with Hormuz scenarios in play; Morgan Stanley's Gower still sees $5,000+ in H2 2027.

items.title: Gold falls to near $4,150 as higher Treasury yields, oil prices outweigh softer PCE inflation
items.summary: Gold tumbled to near $4,150 in early Asian trading Thursday as the 10-year Treasury yield held at 5.298% and the 30-year at 5.642%, overwhelming relief from cooler US inflation data. August headline PCE was 3.4% and core 3.0%, below forecasts, but rising oil prices and hawkish Fed comments kept bullion under pressure. OCBC noted a seven-week low; traders await Friday's US jobs report.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield rises to new 24-year high, posts largest quarterly gain since 1994
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.304% on Wednesday, its highest since May 2002, after US Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% and August PCE inflation held at 3.4%. The 30-year touched about 5.65%, and the 10-year posted its largest quarterly gain since 1994 — nearly 0.9 points. Traders now see only about a 37% chance of an October Fed hike.

items.title: Yields, dollar hold key to gold, silver trajectory in H2FY27: Apurva Seth
items.summary: SAMCO Securities' Apurva Sheth says US real yields, the dollar and central-bank policy expectations will decide whether gold's correction deepens or becomes the launch pad for the next leg higher. Gold has fallen about 11% since April to the $4,100–$4,200 zone from record highs above $5,600; he sees a technically plausible recovery toward $4,600 if real yields fall.

items.title: Will festive season revive gold jewellery demand as prices remain 9% above last year?
items.summary: Gold jewellery demand may rise during India's festive and wedding season, but high prices could push buyers towards lighter designs, gold exchange and value-focused jewellery purchases.

items.title: Poor man's gold may become India's next big story as the silver horse rises
items.summary: Silver is gaining ground in India as record gold prices push consumers towards a more affordable precious metal. Prices have surged 160% in two years, boosting interest in jewellery, gifting and investment; jewellers report rising demand among younger buyers, though high prices remain a constraint.

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Gower sees gold back above $5,000 in H2 2027; silver's run to $120 driven by more than hype
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's Amy Gower told CNBC she expects gold to trade back above $5,000 an ounce within a year, citing strong ETF and central-bank demand despite 20-year-high long-dated yields and dollar strength. She said silver's surge to $120 was driven by fundamentals rather than hype, and pointed to China's record gold imports and Golden Week buying as support.

items.title: Rupee to fall more, yield curve to shift higher in H2FY27: Gaura Sengupta
items.summary: IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta expects the rupee to depreciate further in H2FY27 as RBI intervention turns more cautious now that the FCNR(B) window has closed — the $133 billion mobilised is borrowed money to be repaid in three years. Persistent dollar strength and high US yields keep foreign capital away, pushing the G-sec yield curve higher.

items.title: Gold down 8.5% and silver 13.5% in September as real yields re-price at the fastest pace in four years
items.summary: Gold and silver closed out a bruising September down 8.5% and 13.5% respectively, despite a Wednesday spike to $4,218 and $61.50 on softer US inflation data that erased itself within hours. Inflation-protected US Treasury yields jumped the fastest in four years, adding 0.44 points to the real 10-year rate close to a record high. September's nonfarm payrolls report is due Friday.

items.title: Natixis sees gold price falling to $4,100 by year-end, but three scenarios remain in play
items.summary: Natixis expects gold to remain under pressure through year-end as rising oil prices, persistent inflation and higher rates weigh on the metal, but analyst Bernard Dahdah says the outlook could diverge dramatically depending on how the Strait of Hormuz conflict evolves — laying out three scenarios.

items.title: Dollar wraps best month since March on Fed's inflation fight
items.summary: The US dollar wrapped its best month since March as the Federal Reserve's inflation fight kept rate-hike expectations alive and pushed Treasury yields to multi-decade highs. A firm dollar raises the cost of bullion for buyers in other currencies, adding pressure on gold and silver. The dollar index approached a yearly peak even as softer PCE data trimmed October hike odds.

items.title: MCX bullion steadies after sharp correction; 24K gold Rs 1,49,570
items.summary: Domestic bullion steadied after a sharp correction: 24K gold was at Rs 1,49,570 per 10g (+0.52%), 22K at Rs 1,37,100, 18K at Rs 1,12,180, and silver at Rs 2,26,190 a kg. Global cues, a weaker rupee and pre-festive buying cushioned the downside. Gold support at Rs 1,45,500-1,46,800, resistance at Rs 1,52,000; silver support at Rs 2,24,500, resistance at Rs 2,32,000. Add 3% GST to quoted prices.

items.title: Gold, silver futures rise on MCX on Sept 30
items.summary: MCX gold futures traded 0.64% higher at ₹1,49,810 per 10 grams on September 30, while silver futures were 0.43% higher at ₹2,26,270 per kg. In the physical bullion market, gold was quoted at ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams and silver at ₹2.26 lakh per kg.

items.title: SGB premature redemption dates in October 2026: check tranche-wise dates and deadlines
items.summary: The RBI has disclosed premature-redemption dates for Sovereign Gold Bonds running from October 2026 to March 2027. Investors holding eligible tranches should note the allocated timeframes for submitting their redemption requests — premature redemption is available after five years at the prevailing market price, and missing a window means waiting for the next redemption date.

items.title: High gold prices and steep taxes push more Indian buyers toward off-the-books cash deals
items.summary: Mint reports that soaring gold prices and the import duty hike to 15% (plus 3% GST) are driving more buyers into under-the-counter cash sales without invoices, where bulk buyers can save up to 6%. The shift toward the grey market ahead of the wedding season is an unintended consequence of the policy meant to curb bullion purchases and protect forex reserves.
